text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Sweden's Banverket group won the contract for the railroad stretch between Copenhagen Main Rail Station, Kastrup (Copenhagen International Airport) and Sweden for the new rail-road, tunnel-bridge fixed link between the Danish capital and Malmo, the third biggest Swedish city. The fixed link over the sound waterway between Denmark and Sweden is due to open in the year 2000.

--Danish prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen criticises France for refusing to back a United Nations Human Rights Commission resolution to be tabled by Denmark condemning China for breaches of human rights. Denmark has the support of most European Union member states and the United States. Rasmussen described the French refusal to back the resolution as weakening joint EU foreign policy.

--Denmark's Social Democratic-led government is to launch a 13-point social welfare programme to keep the country in the vanguard as a welfare state. The programme, to be announced within the next few weeks, calls for fewer Danes to take passive state aid.

--Leading multinational firms have launched an attack on Denmark's Tele Danmark telecommunications group for allegedly overcharging by up to 500 percent for telephony and other services. Tele Danmark rejects the charges.
